ownership.quote: Founded by best friends Rob (founding engineer at Substack) and Ben (early engineer at Stripe). We're based in Brooklyn and San Francisco.

stage.quote: We're backed by great institutional investors including Lightspeed, Decibel, Craft, as well as angels like the Collisons, Guillermo Rauch, Chris Best, Immad Akund, Iqram Magdon-Ismali, Andrew Kortina, Charlie Songhurst, and Clem Delangue.
stage.note: Company's own team page confirms institutional VCs (Lightspeed, Decibel, Craft) plus a long list of prominent angels, which is typical of a seed round, but no press release, Crunchbase/Tracxn snapshot, or company statement with a specific round type, amount, or date could be found (Crunchbase and Tracxn pages were blocked/not indexed; no YC or other accelerator affiliation found — https://www.ycombinator.com/companies/zo-computer returns 404). Stage is inferred, not confirmed.

note: Zo Computer (legal entity name appears as 'Substrate Labs Inc.' per the copyright line on the company's own zocomputer.substack.com blog, while the website's schema.org markup lists legalName 'Zo Computer Company'; treat the exact legal name as unconfirmed). Founded 2024 by Rob Cheung (ex-Substack) and Ben Guo (ex-Stripe), based in Brooklyn/NYC and San Francisco. It sells an always-on personal cloud computer/subscription product (Basic/Pro/Ultra plans), not a developer sandbox API — a different buyer profile than most providers in this dataset. Standard search engines (DuckDuckGo, Bing, Google) returned unrelated/garbled results for this query in the research environment, and Crunchbase/LinkedIn/Tracxn were blocked (403/bot-protection); direct fetches of the company's own site and blog were used as the primary evidence instead.
